ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB=AC$, point D is a point inside $\triangle ABC$, $\angle D=110^\circ$, $\angle 1=\angle 2$, then what is the measure of $\angle A$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $\angle D=110^\circ$ and $\angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
it follows that $\angle D=180^\circ-\angle 1-\angle DCB=110^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle 1+\angle DCB=70^\circ$,\\
Since $AB=AC$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$,\\
thus $\angle ABD=\angle BCD$,\\
Since $\angle 1+\angle DCB=70^\circ$ and $\angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB=\angle 2+\angle DCB=70^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle ABC+\angle ACB=140^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle A=180^\circ-140^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB=AC$, point $D$ is inside $\triangle ABC$, $\angle D=110^\circ$, and $\angle 1=\angle 2$. What is the measure of $\angle A$ in degrees?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $\angle D=110^\circ$ and $\angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
it follows that $\angle D=180^\circ-\angle 1-\angle DCB=110^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle 1+\angle DCB=70^\circ$,\\
Since $AB=AC$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$,\\
thus $\angle ABD=\angle BCD$,\\
Since $\angle 1+\angle DCB=70^\circ$ and $\angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB=\angle 2+\angle DCB=70^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle ABC+\angle ACB=140^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle A=180^\circ-140^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$
